summary: The fetch module copies files from remote hosts to the controller in a per-hostname tree. Using become doubles the transfer via slurp and can exhaust memory, and missing files now fail by default.
questions: How do I copy a file from remote servers back to the control node?
Why does fetch use so much memory with become?
How are fetched files organized locally?
How do I avoid fetch failing on a missing file?
Does fetch work with Windows hosts?

answer_card.title: Fetch files from remote hosts
answer_card.answer_md:
`ansible.builtin.fetch` is reverse `copy`: pulls files from remote hosts and stores them locally under a hostname-based tree. Overwrites if different. Works on Windows.

- With `become`, `slurp` is also used, doubling transfer and possibly causing `MemoryError`; avoid `become` when you can.
- Since 2.5 it fails if the file can't be read; use `fail_on_missing: false`, `failed_when`, or `ignore_errors` to change that.
